name: National Institutes of Health
what: NIH describes itself as the largest public funder of biomedical research in the world [117](#cite:117). It is made up of 27 [institutes and centers](#term:institute-or-center), each with its own research agenda [143](#cite:143). Its public budget page says nearly 82 percent of its funding goes out as extramural awards to universities, medical schools and other research institutions, a share computed on FY 2023 figures [56](#cite:56). In FY 2025 it spent more than $26.5 billion on research project grants [27](#cite:27). Organizations that receive NIH grants can be domestic or foreign, public or private, non-profit or for-profit [117](#cite:117).
how_it_decides: Review has two levels: a [scientific review group](#term:study-section) (study section) first, then the [national advisory council](#term:advisory-council) or board of the institute that would pay [38](#cite:38). Since 2025 the [Center for Scientific Review (CSR)](#term:center-for-scientific-review) organizes first-level review of all NIH applications; before that, 23 institute review branches handled about 22 percent of them [55](#cite:55) [54](#cite:54) [40](#cite:40). For most research project codes, reviewers use the simplified framework in force for due dates from January 25, 2025: Importance of the Research and Rigor and Feasibility are each scored 1 to 9, and Expertise and Resources is rated sufficient or insufficient [39](#cite:39) [41](#cite:41). Under modifications that began after the October 2025 lapse in [appropriations](#term:appropriations-act) and now run through the January 2027 council round, about 30-35 percent of applications are discussed, a middle third is labelled 'competitive but not discussed', and [summary statements](#term:summary-statement) are shortened [126](#cite:126) [16](#cite:16) [84](#cite:84). The council makes recommendations and the institute or center director decides [38](#cite:38) [15](#cite:15). Under the unified funding strategy, effective with the January 2026 council round, institutes do not rely on [paylines](#term:payline); each weighs mission alignment, scientific merit read from the whole review, breadth of topics, career stage, broad distribution and geographic balance of funding, and available funds, and each publishes the factors it uses [123](#cite:123) [13](#cite:13) [67](#cite:67).
cycle: NIH runs three review cycles a year [2](#cite:2). Cycle I applications are due January 25 to May 7, reviewed in June-July, go to council in August or October and start in September or December at the earliest; Cycle II applications are due May 25 to September 7, reviewed in October-November, go to council in January and start in April; Cycle III applications are due September 25 to January 7, reviewed in February-March, go to council in May and start in July [2](#cite:2). The federal fiscal year starts October 1, and NIH began FY 2027 under a [continuing resolution](#term:continuing-resolution) that runs through December 11, 2026 [83](#cite:83). NIH's yearly fiscal-policy and legislative-mandate notices follow the full-year appropriation; for FY 2026 they came out on March 18, 2026 [21](#cite:21) [62](#cite:62).
who_to_talk_to: Applicants are sent first to their own organization's [sponsored programmes office](#term:sponsored-programs-office) [146](#cite:146) [119](#cite:119). At NIH, programme officials handle the scientific and programmatic side and can say whether a plan fits their institute; scientific review officers manage [peer review](#term:merit-review); grants management officers and specialists handle the business side [117](#cite:117) [120](#cite:120) [106](#cite:106). A programme official is found through the Matchmaker tool, Section VII of a funding notice, or an institute's profile page [120](#cite:120). Programme officials do not co-write applications or discuss receipt, referral or review details [92](#cite:92). System problems go to the eRA Service Desk [146](#cite:146).
where_it_posts: From fiscal year 2026 [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) is NIH's single official source for grant and [cooperative agreement](#term:cooperative-agreement) funding opportunities; NIH no longer posts them in the NIH Guide for Grants and Contracts, which continues for policy and informational notices [9](#cite:9) [10](#cite:10). NIH's Explore NIH Opportunities tool searches Grants.gov with NIH-specific filters [93](#cite:93) [105](#cite:105). The [parent announcements](#term:parent-announcement) are listed on one NIH page [1](#cite:1). Highlighted Topics name research areas an institute wants to see; they are not funding opportunities, and an application answering one goes in through a parent announcement or another broad notice [11](#cite:11) [142](#cite:142).

name: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases
what: NIAID is one of [NIH](#term:nih)'s institutes [143](#cite:143). Its funding-policy page states rules that go beyond the NIH-wide ones [68](#cite:68).
how_it_decides: NIAID says it no longer uses a score cut-off as the basis for funding; it weighs the [peer review](#term:merit-review) assessment, investigator status, balance across its strategic plan, and the investigator's other active funding, and aims for a [success rate](#term:success-rate) for early stage and [new investigators](#term:early-stage-investigator) at or above that of established investigators [68](#cite:68).

who_to_talk_to: NIAID strongly encourages consultation with its staff at least 15 weeks before a P01 due date and at least 10 weeks before a clinical trial [U01](#term:u01) submission [113](#cite:113) [116](#cite:116).
where_it_posts: On [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), like all NIH institutes [9](#cite:9).

name: National Cancer Institute
what: NCI is one of [NIH](#term:nih)'s institutes [143](#cite:143). It follows the NIH Unified Funding Strategy and publishes the reductions it applies to requested budgets [66](#cite:66) [69](#cite:69).
how_it_decides: NCI no longer uses [paylines](#term:payline) to choose competing [grants](#term:grant); it weighs scientific merit, public health significance, novelty, portfolio representation, career stage and the investigator's funding level [69](#cite:69).
cycle: New [R01](#term:r01) and [U01](#term:u01) awards at or under $250,000 in direct costs are reduced by 6.5% (at or under $175,000) or 8.5% (over $175,000); new R01 and U01 awards over $250,000 are reduced by 17%; [R21](#term:r21-r03) awards by 6.5% or 8.5%; new P01, UM1 and R33 awards by 13% or 17%; [renewals](#term:renewal) are funded at an NCI cap [69](#cite:69).
where_it_posts: NCI states that all [notices of funding opportunity](#term:nofo) are posted by NIH on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) [66](#cite:66).

name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
what: NHLBI is one of [NIH](#term:nih)'s institutes [143](#cite:143). Its funding-policy page sets a shorter funded period for most competing [R01s](#term:r01) than the five-year maximum in the [parent notice](#term:parent-announcement) [70](#cite:70) [4](#cite:4).
how_it_decides: NHLBI states it has no [payline](#term:payline) or strict score cut-off; decisions rest on scientific and technical merit, its [advisory council](#term:advisory-council)'s recommendations, relevance to its strategic priorities, portfolio balance, workforce development and potential public health impact [70](#cite:70).
cycle: NHLBI funds approved investigator-initiated competing R01 applications for up to four years, with exceptions that include [early stage investigators](#term:early-stage-investigator), clinical studies and clinical trials; it gives no inflationary increases for future years [70](#cite:70).
where_it_posts: On [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), like all NIH institutes [9](#cite:9).

name: National Institute of General Medical Sciences
what: NIGMS is one of [NIH](#term:nih)'s institutes [143](#cite:143). It runs the Maximizing Investigators' Research Award (MIRA), an R35 that supports an investigator's whole NIGMS-relevant programme through one [grant](#term:grant) [72](#cite:72) [73](#cite:73).
how_it_decides: NIGMS generally prioritises funding MIRA over [R01](#term:r01) awards, is unlikely to award more than one NIGMS R01 to a [PI](#term:principal-investigator), and needs council approval when an investigator's total annual costs exceed $1.5 million; [early stage investigator](#term:early-stage-investigator) status is one of the factors it lists [71](#cite:71).
cycle: MIRA has its own due dates in January and May (established and new investigators) and in October and February (early stage investigators) [73](#cite:73) [74](#cite:74).
who_to_talk_to: NIGMS gives two MIRA mailboxes, one for established and new investigators and one for early stage investigators [72](#cite:72).
where_it_posts: On [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), like all NIH institutes [9](#cite:9).

name: U.S. National Science Foundation
parent: none stated on the pages read
what: NSF funds research and education across science and engineering through grants, [cooperative agreements](#term:cooperative-agreement) and fellowships [155](#cite:155). It is organised in eight [directorates](#term:nsf-directorate): BIO, CISE, ENG, GEO, MPS, SBE, STEM Education (EDU) and TIP [167](#cite:167). NSF states that it receives approximately 43,000 proposals a year and makes roughly 8,300 awards [152](#cite:152).
how_it_decides: Every proposal is judged on two criteria approved by the National Science Board, [Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts](#term:intellectual-merit) [157](#cite:157) [160](#cite:160). A [programme officer](#term:program-officer) checks the proposal, obtains reviews from ad hoc reviewers, a panel or both, and recommends award or decline; the PAPPG as printed places final programmatic approval at division or office level, followed by a business review in the Division of Grants and Agreements [157](#cite:157). Since December 8, 2025 a full proposal must have at least two reviewers, who may be NSF staff [149](#cite:149). In December 2025 NSF realigned its divisions into sections, clusters or thematic areas to reduce layers, and the pages read do not name the post that now gives programmatic approval [168](#cite:168) [177](#cite:177). [Executive Order 14332](#term:executive-order-14332) requires senior-appointee review of funding announcements and [discretionary awards](#term:discretionary-grant) at every agency [246](#cite:246). NSF returns without review proposals it judges not aligned with agency priorities [154](#cite:154).
cycle: NSF aims to give a decision within six months of submission and generally issues an award to an academic institution within 30 days of the recommendation [160](#cite:160) [165](#cite:165). Twelve foundational-research notices posted in August 2026 mostly accept proposals at any time; other [solicitations](#term:program-solicitation) keep deadlines, target dates or windows [192](#cite:192) [156](#cite:156) [189](#cite:189). MPS Materials counts its one-proposal limit by fiscal year, beginning October 1 [215](#cite:215).
who_to_talk_to: Each funding opportunity lists one or more programme officers, and NSF staff hold webinars and office hours [158](#cite:158). The 2026 core solicitations give a mailbox for each programme, for example bio-fl@nsf.gov and eccs-epmqd@nsf.gov [183](#cite:183) [200](#cite:200). Policy questions go to policy@nsf.gov and system questions to the [Research.gov](#term:research-gov) help desk [165](#cite:165).
where_it_posts: NSF posts opportunities in its Funding Search at nsf.gov/funding/opportunities, on directorate pages, and on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) [155](#cite:155). It publishes four kinds of notice: programme descriptions, programme announcements, programme solicitations and [Dear Colleague Letters](#term:dear-colleague-letter); it also uses [Broad Agency Announcements](#term:broad-agency-announcement) for some use-inspired work [156](#cite:156) [158](#cite:158).

what: ARPA-E funds energy technology research through programme notices, mostly by [cooperative agreement](#term:cooperative-agreement), with teams that may include universities, non-profits, firms and laboratories [301](#cite:301). Its own web pages returned no readable text in this sweep, so this record rests on its notices [301](#cite:301) [302](#cite:302).
how_it_decides: In stages: [concept paper](#term:concept-outline), full application, reviewer comments and the applicant's reply, then selection and negotiation [301](#cite:301). Notices print weighted criteria; in OPEN 2018 impact, merit and team each carried 30% and the management plan 10% [303](#cite:303).
cycle: By programme; no fixed yearly calendar was found [301](#cite:301).
who_to_talk_to: Questions go to ARPA-E by the dates in each notice, and answers are published in a question-and-answer file [301](#cite:301) [302](#cite:302).
where_it_posts: The consolidated DOE eXCHANGE at exchange.energy.gov; the former ARPA-E eXCHANGE address shows a decommission notice [305](#cite:305) [306](#cite:306). Notices also appear on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) [304](#cite:304).

name: Office of Naval Research (ONR)
parent: Department of the Navy, Department of Defense (styled Department of War on some pages)
what: ONR, founded in 1946, funds science and technology research for the Navy and Marine Corps through five science departments [337](#cite:337). Universities, non-profits and commercial entities may receive its [grants](#term:grant) [336](#cite:336).
how_it_decides: [Programme officers](#term:program-officer) assess [white papers](#term:pre-application) and proposals against scientific and technical merit, Naval relevance and available funds, stated as equally important [334](#cite:334).
cycle: The long-range announcement is open continuously; special announcements such as MURI have yearly dates [316](#cite:316) [335](#cite:335).
who_to_talk_to: The cognizant ONR programme officer for the technology area, before a white paper is written [334](#cite:334).
where_it_posts: [SAM.gov](#term:sam-gov) and [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), with a running list on ONR's own announcements page [318](#cite:318) [335](#cite:335).

name: Air Force Office of Scientific Research (AFOSR)
parent: Air Force Research Laboratory, Department of the Air Force
what: AFOSR plans and runs the Air Force Research Laboratory's basic research programme [320](#cite:320). It reports 1,200 [grants](#term:grant) at more than 200 academic institutions [340](#cite:340).
how_it_decides: [Programme officers](#term:program-officer) in two science departments manage the research areas and review proposals under the open announcement [320](#cite:320) [339](#cite:339).
cycle: One open announcement, replaced when superseded; the FY 2025 announcement closed on March 23, 2026 and the next was posted June 4, 2026 [319](#cite:319) [320](#cite:320).
who_to_talk_to: The programme officer for the research area named in the announcement; the announcement mailbox is afosr.baa@us.af.mil [339](#cite:339) [320](#cite:320).
where_it_posts: [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) [322](#cite:322).

name: Army Research Office (ARO), DEVCOM Army Research Laboratory
parent: U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command, Department of the Army
what: ARO is the Army's extramural basic research arm; it was founded in 1951 and works with more than 7,000 researchers and 300 institutions of higher learning [342](#cite:342). Its awards are made mainly as [grants](#term:grant) and [cooperative agreements](#term:cooperative-agreement) [341](#cite:341).
how_it_decides: Against scientific and technical merit, contribution to the Army mission, and the qualifications of the investigators [341](#cite:341).
cycle: Year-round under the ARL [broad agency announcement](#term:broad-agency-announcement), open to November 20, 2027 [324](#cite:324) [342](#cite:342).
who_to_talk_to: An ARL technical point of contact or ARO programme manager, before a whitepaper [341](#cite:341) [342](#cite:342).
where_it_posts: [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) and the ARL announcement page [324](#cite:324) [323](#cite:323).

name: Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA)
parent: Department of Defense (DARPA writes Department of War)
what: [DARPA](#term:darpa) describes itself as an independent research and development agency within the U.S. Department of War, with six technical offices [343](#cite:343). It funds universities among others, through programme [solicitations](#term:program-solicitation) and office-wide announcements [345](#cite:345) [344](#cite:344).
how_it_decides: Programme managers define programmes and choose performers; office-wide announcements take ideas outside current programmes [343](#cite:343) [344](#cite:344).
cycle: Each office keeps an office-wide announcement open for about a year or more; programme solicitations appear as programmes start [347](#cite:347) [344](#cite:344).
who_to_talk_to: Programme managers, reached at Proposers Day events; DARPAConnect offers proposal support [345](#cite:345).
where_it_posts: [SAM.gov](#term:sam-gov) and [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), linked from DARPA's site [344](#cite:344) [347](#cite:347).

name: Basic Research Office, Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering
parent: Department of Defense (styled Department of War on some pages)
what: The Basic [Research Office](#term:sponsored-programs-office) describes itself as working with academia, industry and government partners to shape priorities in scientific investment areas, and as overseeing programmes across the components and universities [349](#cite:349). The cross-service university programmes in this sweep, MURI and Minerva, sit under it; the service research offices issue the MURI announcement and make the awards [325](#cite:325) [329](#cite:329).
how_it_decides: For MURI, each topic's Research Topic Chief in ONR, ARO or AFOSR assesses [white papers](#term:pre-application) and proposals against the announcement's criteria [325](#cite:325).
cycle: MURI runs once a year; the FY 2027 announcement was posted September 21, 2026 [326](#cite:326).
who_to_talk_to: The Research Topic Chief named for the MURI topic [325](#cite:325).
where_it_posts: [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), under the announcement numbers of the three service offices [325](#cite:325) [326](#cite:326).

name: Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs (CDMRP)
parent: Defense Health Agency Research and Development – Medical Research and Development Command, Department of Defense (styled Department of War in FY26 announcements)
what: [CDMRP](#term:cdmrp) began in 1992 with a congressional [appropriation](#term:appropriations-act) and funds biomedical research in programmes named by Congress [350](#cite:350). Its money is added by Congress each year and is not in the [President's budget request](#term:budget-request) [351](#cite:351). Universities, medical schools, non-profits, firms and foreign organisations may apply as extramural organisations [330](#cite:330).
how_it_decides: Two tiers: [peer review](#term:merit-review) for scientific merit and impact, then programmatic review for fit with the programme's vision and portfolio; consumer reviewers vote in both [352](#cite:352).
cycle: Yearly, following the defense appropriation. FY 2025: $650 million for 12 programmes under a full-year continuing resolution signed March 15, 2025 [353]. FY 2026: $1.27 billion for 34 programmes under an act signed February 3, 2026 [295](#cite:295).
who_to_talk_to: The [eBRAP](#term:ebrap) help desk, (301) 682-5507 or help@eBRAP.org, for questions on announcements and submission [358](#cite:358) [331](#cite:331).
where_it_posts: The CDMRP website, [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) and eBRAP [295](#cite:295).

name: NASA Science Mission Directorate (SMD)
what: The [directorate](#term:nsf-directorate) funds research in Earth science, planetary science, astrophysics, heliophysics, and biological and physical sciences [399](#cite:399) [390](#cite:390). Most research [grants](#term:grant) come through the yearly [ROSES](#term:roses) [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) [371](#cite:371). Awards are issued and managed by the NASA Shared Services Center [379](#cite:379).
how_it_decides: [Peer review](#term:merit-review) by subject experts against intrinsic merit, programmatic relevance and cost reasonableness, with a selection official deciding [386](#cite:386). Dual-anonymous peer review is the default under ROSES-2025 [375](#cite:375). NASA posts ROSES selection statistics; the newest files are dated July 2025 [378](#cite:378).
cycle: One ROSES a year, amended through the year. ROSES-2025 was released July 10, 2025; ROSES-2026 was announced for July 2026 and had not been found released on the sweep date [372](#cite:372) [294](#cite:294) [395](#cite:395).
who_to_talk_to: The [programme officer](#term:program-officer) for the programme element, from the directorate's list, last updated September 18, 2026 [390](#cite:390).
where_it_posts: [NSPIRES](#term:nspires), with a running page on science.nasa.gov and listings on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) [371](#cite:371) [394](#cite:394).

name: National Institute of Food and Agriculture
what: USDA's extramural funding agency for agricultural research, education and extension. It has three kinds of funding: competitive [grants](#term:grant); capacity grants to [land-grant institutions](#term:land-grant-institution), schools of forestry and schools of veterinary medicine; and non-competitive grants directed by Congress. Its largest competitive programme is the Agriculture and Food Research Initiative [422](#cite:422) [406](#cite:406).
how_it_decides: [Peer review](#term:merit-review) panels rank applications against criteria published with each notice; NIFA's regulation requires scientific peer review or merit review and gives applicants their reviews without reviewer names. After review the [Project Director](#term:principal-investigator) is told of a recommendation, a pre-award administrative review follows, Awards Management approves the award and sets terms, and Financial Management approves the funding. FY 2026 notices add that projects are to align with the five priorities in Secretary's Memorandum 1078-020 [422](#cite:422) [416](#cite:416) [409](#cite:409) [412](#cite:412) [418](#cite:418).
cycle: One notice per programme per fiscal year. For FY 2026 the AFRI Foundational and Applied Science notice was posted August 1, 2025 with December 2025 deadlines; Strengthening Agricultural Systems was posted January 29, 2026; Organic Agriculture Research and Extension March 11, 2026; Specialty Crop Research Initiative April 13, 2026. FY 2027 AFRI deadlines are to be announced in the FY 2027 notices [408](#cite:408) [424](#cite:424).
who_to_talk_to: Each programme area priority has its own contact address (for example A1102@usda.gov), and each notice names programme contacts; the AFRI Coordination Team is the general AFRI contact. Application questions go to GrantApplicationQuestions@usda.gov [404](#cite:404) [403](#cite:403) [421](#cite:421).
where_it_posts: On its own funding opportunities page and on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), through which applications are submitted [408](#cite:408) [409](#cite:409).

name: Agricultural Research Service
what: USDA's in-house research agency. It is not a [grant](#term:grant) competition funder in the usual sense: it works with outside institutions mainly through non-assistance [cooperative agreements](#term:cooperative-agreement) under 7 [CFR](#term:cfr) part 550, entered without competition where a cooperator and the agency share an interest in the research [428](#cite:428) [427](#cite:427).
how_it_decides: By agreement between the agency and a cooperator rather than by a public competition; the rule exempts these agreements from competition requirements [428](#cite:428).
who_to_talk_to: The Financial Management and Agreements Division publishes partnership resources for cooperators and points of contact [427](#cite:427).

name: Forest Service Research and Development
what: Recorded in outline only. The Forest Service's [grants](#term:grant) and agreements page sends applicants to [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) and to regional contacts and does not describe a research grant programme for outside institutions; no such programme was confirmed on a primary page in this sweep [429](#cite:429).
where_it_posts: Grants.gov [429](#cite:429).

This is a request, not enacted law [445](#cite:445) [444](#cite:444).

name: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
what: NOAA funds outside research through several offices: the Office of Oceanic and Atmospheric Research (the Climate Program Office, the Weather Program Office, Sea Grant, Ocean Exploration and the Cooperative Institutes), the National Ocean Service (the NCCOS Competitive Research Program) and NOAA Fisheries. The [research office](#term:sponsored-programs-office) works through ten laboratories, 16 Cooperative Institutes and 34 Sea Grant programmes [444](#cite:444) [430](#cite:430) [442](#cite:442) [437](#cite:437).
how_it_decides: Each notice sets its own [merit review](#term:merit-review). The two 2026 research notices read differ: the Climate Program Office notice uses a peer panel of 4-7 NOAA employees, while the NCCOS notice uses mail review by individual experts followed by an independent peer panel. In both, a Selection Official awards in rank order unless a published selection factor (funding, balance, duplication, programme priorities, past performance) justifies another order. Both notices cite [Executive Orders](#term:executive-order) 14173, 14281 and 14303 [432](#cite:432) [477](#cite:477).
cycle: No single calendar. In 2026 the research notices found were posted on May 5-6 (RISA), September 11 (Earth System Science and Services Partnership), August 24 (bycatch reduction) and September 25 (NCCOS). The annual Climate Program Office and Weather Program Office programme competitions last posted in 2024 [434](#cite:434) [431](#cite:431) [475](#cite:475) [480](#cite:480).
who_to_talk_to: Each notice names a competition or programme manager and a grants specialist. The research office's [broad agency announcement](#term:broad-agency-announcement) told applicants to contact programme staff in the relevant line office before submitting [431](#cite:431) [478](#cite:478).
where_it_posts: On [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), with office pages (Climate Program Office, Sea Grant, NCCOS, NOAA Fisheries) carrying their own notices. Applicants register in [SAM.gov](#term:sam-gov), Grants.gov and [eRA Commons](#term:era-commons), which replaced Grants Online for applications submitted after January 1, 2024 [448](#cite:448) [447](#cite:447).

what: EPA has funded outside research mainly through the Science to Achieve Results (STAR) programme and the P3 student design competition. EPA announced on July 18, 2025 a reduction in force affecting the Office of Research and Development and a new Office of Applied Science and Environmental Solutions. who_to_talk_to: Past STAR notices named a technical contact, an eligibility contact and an electronic submissions contact [462](#cite:462).
where_it_posts: On its Research Funding Opportunities page and on Grants.gov [452](#cite:452) [461](#cite:461).

name: National Institute of Standards and Technology
what: NIST's laboratories fund outside research in measurement science and standards as [grants](#term:grant) or [cooperative agreements](#term:cooperative-agreement), mainly through one multi-laboratory notice (the Measurement Science and Engineering Research Grant Programs) and small named programmes such as the Precision Measurement Grant Program [465](#cite:465) [471](#cite:471).
how_it_decides: Each laboratory or programme reviews applications against criteria in the notice, with a named selecting official. The Precision Measurement notice uses at least three and up to eight independent reviewers and names a division chief as selecting official; the Information Technology Laboratory scores on four criteria for 30 points [471](#cite:471) [467](#cite:467).
cycle: The measurement science notice took applications on a rolling basis until an amendment of June 9, 2026 set a final deadline of September 15, 2026. The Precision Measurement notice is annual (posted February 23, 2026). No research grant notice from NIST is open or [forecast](#term:forecast) on the sweep date [464](#cite:464) [471](#cite:471) [470](#cite:470).
who_to_talk_to: The measurement science notice names a contact for each laboratory and office, and each named programme notice names a technical contact [465](#cite:465) [471](#cite:471).
where_it_posts: On [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov); NIST states that official notices of [solicitations](#term:program-solicitation) are found there [468](#cite:468) [470](#cite:470).

name: US Geological Survey
what: USGS funds outside research that complements its own programmes. The competitive lines found are the Earthquake Hazards Program's external research support, the Water Resources Research Act Program run through 54 state institutes, host agreements for the Climate Adaptation Science Centers, and agreements with partners of the Cooperative Ecosystem Studies Units [490](#cite:490) [481](#cite:481) [483](#cite:483) [489](#cite:489) [487](#cite:487).
how_it_decides: For earthquake hazards research, panels review proposals and sort them into funded, recommended but unfunded, and not recommended. Review for the other programmes is not described on the pages read [481](#cite:481).
cycle: The earthquake hazards announcement is annual (posted April 29, 2026 for FY 2027, due June 4, 2026). Water resources notices post when approved; the FY2026 general competitive notice posted September 30, 2026 [482](#cite:482) [486](#cite:486) [484](#cite:484).
who_to_talk_to: For earthquake hazards, the External Research Manager and the regional and topical coordinators. For water resources, the director of the state Water Resources Research Institute [481](#cite:481) [485](#cite:485).
where_it_posts: On [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) [481](#cite:481) [487](#cite:487).

name: Department of Transportation research grants (Office of the Assistant Secretary for Research and Technology and operating administrations)
what: DOT's main university research programme is the University Transportation Centers Program, run by the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Research and Technology under 49 U.S.C. 5505. The Federal Aviation Administration keeps a standing aviation research [grants](#term:grant) announcement [493](#cite:493) [498](#cite:498).
how_it_decides: For University Transportation Centers, subject matter experts from the research community and DOT rate applications against five statutory criteria, and the Secretary of Transportation makes the final selection [493](#cite:493).
cycle: University Transportation Centers are competed once per authorization, with re-opened competitions for vacant slots; the latest closed in February 2026 [492](#cite:492) [493](#cite:493).
who_to_talk_to: The University Transportation Centers office (UTCgrants@dot.gov; the [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) record names the Acting Director) [493](#cite:493) [494](#cite:494).
where_it_posts: On Grants.gov and the DOT University Transportation Centers pages; applications for the 2025 recompetition went through Valid Eval [492](#cite:492) [493](#cite:493).

name: Department of Homeland Security Science and Technology Directorate, Office of University Programs
what: The office that has run the Centers of Excellence, a Minority Serving Institutions programme and workforce initiatives. Its pages were last updated in 2023, and no DHS university research notice is open or [forecast](#term:forecast) on the sweep date; the current status of its programmes could not be confirmed on a primary page [500](#cite:500) [499](#cite:499) [501](#cite:501).
how_it_decides: Not described on the pages read [499](#cite:499).
where_it_posts: Past Centers of Excellence notices were posted on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) [501](#cite:501).

name: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality
what: AHRQ is the [HHS](#term:hhs) agency for health services research: quality and safety, delivery and practice improvement, and whole-person care are the priorities its funding page names. In March 2026 it ended its standing R01, R03 and R18 announcements and several topic-specific ones early, and on 2026-10-04 its announcement index showed no open opportunities. HHS announced in March 2025 that AHRQ would merge with ASPE into an Office of Strategy, and the FY2027 budget places AHRQ in that office [504](#cite:504) [515](#cite:515) [518](#cite:518) [530](#cite:530) [536](#cite:536).
how_it_decides: Applications were assigned to a [peer review](#term:merit-review) group or special emphasis panel; AHRQ has one chartered Health Services Research Initial Review Group with four [study sections](#term:study-section), working under 42 [CFR](#term:cfr) Part 67, Subpart A. Funding decisions were described as based on merit, priorities and available funds [506](#cite:506) [520](#cite:520) [507](#cite:507).
cycle: The standing calendar had three receipt cycles a year by mechanism (R01 on February 5, June 5 and October 5). No AHRQ announcement was open on 2026-10-04, so the calendar is not in use [505](#cite:505) [518](#cite:518).
who_to_talk_to: AHRQ's contact page lists programme staff by research priority, a [Grants Management Officer](#term:grants-management-officer) and a peer review contact, and states that it welcomes inquiries about current areas of research interest. Whether the listed staff remain after the 2025 reductions was not confirmed [521](#cite:521) [523](#cite:523).
where_it_posts: In the [NIH](#term:nih) Guide for [Grants](#term:grant) and Contracts, with an index on ahrq.gov; special emphasis notices and policy notices carry NOT-HS numbers [518](#cite:518) [519](#cite:519).

name: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (extramural research, including NIOSH and the Injury Center)
what: CDC funds extramural research through its centres and institutes. The two research lines read are the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health, which uses NIH-style [activity codes](#term:activity-code), and the Injury Center, which issues single-year research requests for applications. NIOSH's standing [R01](#term:r01) and [R21](#term:r21-r03) announcements expired on November 21, 2025; its pages of 2026 show only World Trade Center Health Program research as open [552](#cite:552) [556](#cite:556) [551](#cite:551) [560](#cite:560).
how_it_decides: At NIOSH, scientists from outside the agency carry out initial review in the Safety and Occupational Health [Study Section](#term:study-section) or special emphasis panels, and the NIOSH Secondary Review Committee then reviews for programme relevance and portfolio balance [552](#cite:552).
cycle: NIOSH programme announcements typically had three receipt dates a year and requests for applications one. The Injury Center's FY2026 research notice was posted May 29, 2026 [552](#cite:552) [560](#cite:560).
who_to_talk_to: NIOSH routes questions through a web form to three teams; Scientific Program Officials are the primary contact for grantees and Scientific Review Officers answer questions on review. Contacts for each notice are in its Agency Contacts section [553](#cite:553) [552](#cite:552).
where_it_posts: All CDC [grant](#term:grant) and [cooperative agreement](#term:cooperative-agreement) opportunities are posted on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov); NIOSH research announcements also appear in the [NIH](#term:nih) Guide for Grants and Contracts [550](#cite:550) [552](#cite:552).

name: Food and Drug Administration (extramural research grants and cooperative agreements)
what: FDA awards research [grants](#term:grant) and [cooperative agreements](#term:cooperative-agreement) in support of its regulatory work. The lines read are the orphan products clinical trials and natural history grants, the Centers of Excellence in Regulatory Science and Innovation, and single-topic regulatory science cooperative agreements issued by FDA centres [561](#cite:561) [566](#cite:566) [564](#cite:564).
how_it_decides: An objective review committee convened by FDA scores applications against criteria with points set in each notice; the number of awards depends on [appropriations](#term:appropriations-act) and on enough meritorious applications [564](#cite:564) [561](#cite:561).
cycle: The orphan products clinical trials grants have one new-application date each October through 2027; topic-specific notices can open and close within a month [561](#cite:561) [564](#cite:564).
who_to_talk_to: Each notice names a scientific contact in the sponsoring FDA centre and a grants management contact in the Office of Acquisitions and Grants Services; the rare disease programmes have a contact page [564](#cite:564) [567](#cite:567) [563](#cite:563).
where_it_posts: On [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) and in the [NIH](#term:nih) Guide for Grants and Contracts under RFA-FD numbers; applications go through Grants.gov and [eRA Commons](#term:era-commons) [561](#cite:561) [564](#cite:564).

name: Health Resources and Services Administration (maternal and child health research line)
what: HRSA is mainly a service and workforce funder. Its research [grant](#term:grant) line sits in the Maternal and Child Health Bureau's Office of Epidemiology and Research, which has funded field-initiated studies, secondary data analysis studies, research networks and consortia. No open research notice was found on 2026-10-04 [569](#cite:569) [568](#cite:568).

how_it_decides: For NSGP the state agency scores each non-profit's Investment Justification, FEMA reviews eligibility and allowability, multipliers and bonus points are applied, and the Secretary of Homeland Security makes the final decision on [subawards](#term:subaward) [1320](#cite:1320).
cycle: One NSGP notice a year, posted April 16 in 2024, July 28 in 2025 and June 24 in 2026 [1318](#cite:1318).
who_to_talk_to: The [State Administrative Agency](#term:state-administering-agency) for a non-profit; the [FEMA GO](#term:fema-go) Help Desk (1-877-585-3242, femago@fema.dhs.gov) for the state applicant [1319](#cite:1319).
where_it_posts: On [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) and fema.gov; the state applies in FEMA GO [1320](#cite:1320) [1318](#cite:1318).
governing_terms: The DHS Standard Terms and Conditions for the fiscal year; the FY2025 NSGP notice applied version 3 of the FY2025 terms with two paragraphs excluded [1321](#cite:1321).

name: Legal Services Corporation
what: [LSC](#term:legal-services-corporation) is an independent [501(c)(3)](#term:section-501c3) non-profit established by Congress in 1974 and funded by annual [appropriation](#term:appropriations-act). A board of 11 members appointed by the President and confirmed by the Senate governs it. It distributes over 94 percent of its funding to 129 independent non-profit legal aid programmes with more than 800 offices [1328](#cite:1328).
how_it_decides: Basic Field [Grant](#term:grant) applications are assessed against the LSC Act, LSC Regulations, the LSC Performance Criteria and the ABA Standards for the Provision of Civil Legal Aid [1326](#cite:1326).
cycle: Basic Field Grants: [request for proposals](#term:open-call) in April, applications due June 1, decisions announced in December for the following calendar year [1325](#cite:1325) [1324](#cite:1324).
who_to_talk_to: LSC's grant programme staff; the Pro Bono Innovation Fund gives probonoinnovation@lsc.gov [1333](#cite:1333).
where_it_posts: On lsc.gov, with applications in its own system, GrantEase [1324](#cite:1324).
governing_terms: The LSC Act and LSC Regulations, which also bind [subgrants](#term:subaward) of LSC funds [1326](#cite:1326).

name: U.S. Department of Education, elementary, secondary and community programmes (Office of Elementary and Secondary Education)
what: The Department of Education's school and community [grant](#term:grant) programmes include [formula grants](#term:formula-grant) to States, such as 21st Century Community Learning Centers, and discretionary competitions such as the Charter Schools Program, Education Innovation and Research, Full-Service Community Schools and Promise Neighborhoods [1399](#cite:1399) [1453](#cite:1453) [1401](#cite:1401) [1400](#cite:1400) [1395](#cite:1395). Since November 2025 other departments run many of these competitions for Education under interagency agreements [672](#cite:672) [1397](#cite:1397).
how_it_decides: Each competition is governed by its notice inviting applications, which sets absolute and competitive preference priorities [1401](#cite:1401) [1395](#cite:1395). The Secretary's supplemental priorities, effective October 9, 2025, may be used in any discretionary competition whose statute allows it: Promoting Evidence-Based Literacy, Expanding Education Choice, and Returning Education to the States [1392](#cite:1392). Further supplemental priorities were finalised in 2026 on meaningful learning opportunities, career pathways and workforce readiness, artificial intelligence in education, and patriotic education [1393](#cite:1393).
cycle: In 2026 most competition notices were published between late March and early June, with deadlines 30 to 80 days later [1381](#cite:1381) [1382](#cite:1382) [1395](#cite:1395).
who_to_talk_to: Each [Federal Register](#term:federal-register) notice names a programme contact; grantees of the programmes moved to HHS are told to stay in contact with both Education and HHS programme staff [1395](#cite:1395) [1398](#cite:1398).
where_it_posts: A short notice in the Federal Register announces each competition; the full notice inviting applications is on the programme's ed.gov page, on the partner agency's site and on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), where applications are submitted [1382](#cite:1382) [1384](#cite:1384) [1395](#cite:1395).
governing_terms: The Education Department General Administrative Regulations; a [proposed rule](#term:proposed-rule) to revise them was published August 24, 2026 and was not read [1393](#cite:1393).

name: AmeriCorps (Corporation for National and Community Service)
what: AmeriCorps funds organisations to engage members and volunteers in service: State and National [grants](#term:grant), VISTA, and the AmeriCorps Seniors programmes [1374](#cite:1374) [1379](#cite:1379) [1378](#cite:1378). In April 2025 the agency terminated 1,031 grants and placed about 85 percent of its staff on leave; a court enjoined the programme closures in the plaintiff States [1380](#cite:1380). It posted FY 2027 competitions in August 2026 [1375](#cite:1375).
how_it_decides: State and National money is split by regulation between a population formula to States, a competition among States and direct competitive grants [1377](#cite:1377). RSVP grants are chosen competitively with [peer review](#term:merit-review) panels [1378](#cite:1378). The agency renewed its External Reviewer application form in 2026 [1457](#cite:1457).
cycle: The State and National notice is posted in late summer with a January deadline; the FY 2027 RSVP notice was posted August 20, 2026 with an October 20, 2026 deadline [1374](#cite:1374) [1376](#cite:1376).
who_to_talk_to: The listings give americorpsgrants@americorps.gov for State and National and RSVPCompetition@americorps.gov for RSVP [1374](#cite:1374) [1376](#cite:1376).
where_it_posts: On [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), with the full notice and resources on the competition page at americorps.gov [1374](#cite:1374).
governing_terms: 45 [CFR](#term:cfr) chapter XXV, including parts 2521 (State and National), 2553 (RSVP), 2552 (Foster Grandparents) and 2556 (VISTA) [1377](#cite:1377) [1378](#cite:1378) [1451](#cite:1451) [1379](#cite:1379).

name: USDA Rural Development
what: Rural Development makes loans and [grants](#term:grant) for rural community facilities, housing, utilities and business development; its grants to non-profits include Community Facilities grants and the Rural Community Development Initiative [1410](#cite:1410) [1411](#cite:1411).

cycle: Community Facilities applications are taken all year, October 1 to September 30; competitive programmes such as RCDI open by notice in the [Federal Register](#term:federal-register) [1410](#cite:1410) [1411](#cite:1411).

where_it_posts: Programme pages at rd.usda.gov, notices in the Federal Register, and [application packages](#term:application-package) on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) [1411](#cite:1411).

name: USDA Food and Nutrition Service (site now titled Food and Nutrition Administration)
what: The agency runs the federal nutrition programmes and makes a small number of competitive [grants](#term:grant) to organisations, among them the Patrick Leahy Farm to School grants [1414](#cite:1414). On the sweep date its web address fns.usda.gov redirected to fna.usda.gov, where the site is titled Food and Nutrition Administration [1413](#cite:1413).

cycle: The FY 2026 farm to school request was released in September 2025 with a December deadline and awards the following June [1414](#cite:1414).
where_it_posts: On its grant pages and on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), where the request for applications is attached to the listing [1413](#cite:1413) [1414](#cite:1414).

name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (community and education grants)
what: Outside its [research office](#term:sponsored-programs-office), EPA makes [grants](#term:grant) to communities and organisations for environmental education, brownfields assessment, cleanup and job training [1419](#cite:1419) [1420](#cite:1420) [1456](#cite:1456). name: U.S. Economic Development Administration
what: EDA makes [grants](#term:grant) for public works, economic adjustment, planning and technical assistance in economically distressed regions [1430](#cite:1430) [1431](#cite:1431).
how_it_decides: An Investment Review Committee evaluates applications; the share EDA pays depends on the region's distress [1431](#cite:1431) [1432](#cite:1432).
cycle: Its main notices are rolling, with no deadlines, and stay open until replaced, cancelled or exhausted [1430](#cite:1430).

name: National Telecommunications and Information Administration
what: NTIA runs the broadband and digital equity [grant](#term:grant) programmes created in 2021, among them the Digital Equity Act programmes [1425](#cite:1425). The Digital Equity Competitive Grant Program was cancelled on May 9, 2025 and is the subject of a court ruling of July 15, 2026 [1426](#cite:1426).
where_it_posts: On its programme pages; the 2024 competitive applications went through the NTIA Grants Portal [1425](#cite:1425).

name: Community Development Financial Institutions Fund
what: The [CDFI](#term:cdfi) Fund makes awards to certified community development financial institutions, including non-profit loan funds, and runs related programmes [1433](#cite:1433) [1436](#cite:1436).
how_it_decides: The FY 2025 notice describes a staged review: eligibility checks, then evaluation against the criteria in its regulations, then selection and a final compliance check [1434](#cite:1434).
cycle: One notice of funds availability per programme per round. The FY 2025 CDFI Program notice was published in January 2025; FY 2026 notices for the Small Dollar Loan, Bank Enterprise Award and Bond Guarantee programmes were published June 30, 2026 [1434](#cite:1434) [1436](#cite:1436).
who_to_talk_to: Applicants send questions as a service request in AMIS [1435](#cite:1435).
where_it_posts: In the [Federal Register](#term:federal-register) and at cdfifund.gov; applications use [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) for the [SF-424](#term:sf-424) and AMIS for the rest [1434](#cite:1434).

name: Internal Revenue Service (grants to community tax programmes)
what: The IRS makes three kinds of [grant](#term:grant) to organisations that help taxpayers: Volunteer Income Tax Assistance, Tax Counseling for the Elderly, and Low Income Taxpayer Clinics [1437](#cite:1437) [1439](#cite:1439).
cycle: VITA and TCE applications are taken each May; the LITC notice for the next grant year is posted in May with a July deadline [1437](#cite:1437) [1439](#cite:1439).
who_to_talk_to: The VITA Grant Office at grant.program.office@irs.gov; the LITC Program Office through the contact on the listing [1438](#cite:1438) [1439](#cite:1439).
where_it_posts: On [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) and in IRS news releases; LITC applications go through litcgrants.treasury.gov [1437](#cite:1437) [1439](#cite:1439).
how_it_decides: VITA and LITC applications each get a scored technical evaluation followed by a review by the programme office [1460](#cite:1460) [1459](#cite:1459).
policy_guide_note: Publication 3319 governs LITC grants and Publication 4671 governs VITA grants; each is reissued for the grant year [1459](#cite:1459) [1460](#cite:1460).

name: U.S. Small Business Administration (grants to resource partners)
what: SBA gives [grants](#term:grant) and [cooperative agreements](#term:cooperative-agreement) to non-profits, resource partners and educational organisations that counsel and train entrepreneurs; it gives none for starting or expanding a business [1441](#cite:1441). The programmes it names include Small Business Development Centers, Women's Business Centers, SCORE, Veterans Business Outreach Centers, the State Trade Expansion Program, FAST and PRIME [1441](#cite:1441).
where_it_posts: Its grants page lists the programmes; Women's Business Center funding is announced by a programme announcement each fiscal year [1441](#cite:1441) [1443](#cite:1443).
governing_terms: 13 [CFR](#term:cfr) part 130 for Small Business Development Centers and part 131 for Women's Business Centers [1442](#cite:1442) [1443](#cite:1443).

name: Appalachian Regional Commission
what: ARC is a federal-state partnership that makes [grants](#term:grant) for economic development in the Appalachian Region [1444](#cite:1444). Its grants go to state and local governments, tribes, [institutions of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education) and non-profits, never to individuals or for-profit entities [1444](#cite:1444).
how_it_decides: Area Development applications are reviewed and approved by the State first and then by ARC, ending with the Federal Co-Chair; applications to ARISE, POWER, INSPIRE and READY go to ARC first and then to state review [1444](#cite:1444).
cycle: Area Development deadlines vary by state [1445](#cite:1445).
who_to_talk_to: The state ARC programme manager [1445](#cite:1445).
where_it_posts: On arc.gov, by initiative [1444](#cite:1444).

name: Delta Regional Authority
what: The Delta Regional Authority makes investments in infrastructure, business development and workforce development through programmes such as SEDAP [1447](#cite:1447).
cycle: The 2026 SEDAP cycle opened June 1 and closed July 31, 2026 [1447](#cite:1447).
who_to_talk_to: The Local Development District for the applicant's area; technical questions to sedap.cif@dra.gov [1447](#cite:1447).
where_it_posts: On its programme pages at dra.gov [1447](#cite:1447).

what: The Office of Integrative Activities sits in the [NSF](#term:nsf) Office of the Director and runs the NSF-wide capacity programmes: EPSCoR, GRANTED, Growing Convergence Research, Major Research Instrumentation, Mid-scale RI-1 and the Science and Technology Centers [1578](#cite:1578). name: NIH Office of Research Infrastructure Programs (ORIP), Division of Construction and Instruments
what: ORIP's Division of Construction and Instruments runs [NIH](#term:nih)'s three infrastructure programmes: C06 extramural construction, [S10](#term:s10) instrumentation, and S15 equipment (formerly under the R24 [activity code](#term:activity-code)) [1538](#cite:1538).

cycle: ORIP issues S10 notices with one annual receipt date; the C06 notice has one receipt date a year, in January from 2027 [1535](#cite:1535) [1541](#cite:1541).

name: NIGMS Division for Research Capacity Building (IDeA)
what: The Division for Research Capacity Building at the National Institute of General Medical Sciences administers the [Institutional Development Award](#term:idea-program) (IDeA) programme [1543](#cite:1543). IDeA is congressionally mandated and builds research capacity in states that have had low levels of [NIH](#term:nih) funding; it has five components: COBRE, INBRE, the clinical and translational research programmes, co-funding, and the regional entrepreneurship programme I-RED [1543](#cite:1543).
how_it_decides: COBRE applications go to a [Scientific Review Group](#term:study-section) and only the top half are discussed [1545](#cite:1545). Co-funding is decided once a year from [nominations](#term:institutional-nomination) by NIH institutes, with decisions typically in June or July [1553](#cite:1553).
cycle: COBRE has three due dates a year; INBRE is competed once every several years, with the next notice [forecast](#term:forecast) for February 2027 [1545](#cite:1545) [1549](#cite:1549).
who_to_talk_to: The IDeA page points to the division's staff contacts and gives the NIGMS telephone number 301-496-7301 [1543](#cite:1543).
where_it_posts: On the NIGMS programme pages and on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) [1544](#cite:1544) [1551](#cite:1551).

what: NCATS leads the Clinical and Translational Science Awards programme, a national network of more than 60 medical institutions [1557](#cite:1557). Its list of active funding opportunities on October 4, 2026 showed parent fellowship announcements and NIH-wide policy notices and no institutional capacity notice [1623](#cite:1623).

name: House Committee on Appropriations (Community Project Funding)
what: The Committee writes the House's annual appropriations bills and runs the House side of the [earmark](#term:community-project-funding) process, which it calls Community Project Funding [1667](#cite:1667). It does not take applications from organisations: only a Member may submit a request, and the money, if enacted, is awarded by the federal agency whose account the project sits in [1667](#cite:1667) [1672](#cite:1672).
how_it_decides: Each Member may submit at most 20 requests across all bills, with a written federal nexus statement and evidence of community support for each [1667](#cite:1667). Each subcommittee publishes the accounts it will take requests in and the kinds of recipient and project it will consider [1668](#cite:1668) [1669](#cite:1669). Total Community Project Funding will not exceed one half of one percent of discretionary spending [1667](#cite:1667).
cycle: For FY27 the subcommittee deadlines for Members ran from March 13 to March 27, 2026, and Members had to post their requests online by dates from March 27 to April 17, 2026 [1668](#cite:1668). For FY26 the Transportation-HUD deadline was May 23, 2025 [1707](#cite:1707).
who_to_talk_to: The office of the organisation's own Member of the House, which sets its own earlier deadline and form; the Committee requires each Member to post every request online [1666](#cite:1666) [1667](#cite:1667).
where_it_posts: Guidance by subcommittee on its Member requests guidance page, and tables of requested and included projects on its Community Project Funding page [1668](#cite:1668) [1666](#cite:1666).
governing_terms: The Committee's general guidance for the fiscal year and each subcommittee's guidance [1667](#cite:1667) [1668](#cite:1668).

name: Senate Committee on Appropriations (Congressionally Directed Spending)
what: The Committee writes the Senate's annual [appropriations](#term:appropriations-act) bills and runs the Senate side of the [earmark](#term:community-project-funding) process, which it calls Congressionally Directed Spending [1674](#cite:1674). Only a Senator may submit a request; the Committee considers only requests that meet its rules and that it judges appropriate for federal support [1674](#cite:1674).
how_it_decides: Funding for these items may not exceed one percent of discretionary spending, for-profit entities are ineligible, and each Senator certifies that neither the Senator nor immediate family has a financial interest in a requested item [1675](#cite:1675). Each subcommittee sets a per-Senator limit on requests, from 10 in Homeland Security to 65 in Labor-HHS-Education and in Transportation-HUD [1675](#cite:1675). Rule XLIV of the Standing Rules of the Senate applies [1676](#cite:1676).
cycle: For FY27 the subcommittee deadlines for Senators ran from April 7 to May 7, 2026 [1675](#cite:1675). Senators post their requests on their websites within 15 calendar days of the subcommittee deadline [1676](#cite:1676). The same certification and posting rules applied in the FY2026 cycle [1678](#cite:1678).
who_to_talk_to: The offices of the organisation's two Senators, each of which sets its own deadline and form and must publish its requests and certification on its website [1674](#cite:1674).
where_it_posts: General guidance and a chart of requests on its page for the fiscal year; tables of projects in Senate bills and in enacted laws on its Congressionally Directed Spending page for the fiscal year [1674](#cite:1674) [1677](#cite:1677).
governing_terms: The Committee's general guidance for the fiscal year and its reforms and regulations document, which this sweep could not read [1675](#cite:1675) [1674](#cite:1674).

name: National Park Service, State, Tribal, Local, Plans & Grants Division (Historic Preservation Fund grants)
what: This division of the National Park Service runs the Historic Preservation Fund's [grants](#term:grant): [formula grants](#term:formula-grant) to State and Tribal Historic Preservation Offices, competitive project grants and disaster recovery grants [1691](#cite:1691) [1692](#cite:1692). The competitive programmes are African American Civil Rights, Save America's Treasures, Paul Bruhn Historic Revitalization, History of Equal Rights, Semiquincentennial, [HBCU](#term:hbcu), Underrepresented Communities and Tribal Heritage grants [1694](#cite:1694).
how_it_decides: National Park Service personnel, and in some cases independent reviewers, score applications against the criteria in each notice; the Save America's Treasures notice uses four criteria at 25 points each [1705](#cite:1705).

Not funded: individuals, including scholarships and fellowships; political, labor and fraternal organisations and civic clubs; government and municipal agencies; endowment funds; [fiscally sponsored](#term:fiscal-sponsorship) organisations; individual pre-K-12 schools; memorial campaigns; sports; travel; books, films, videos or television programmes [2439](#cite:2439). Funding outside the United States is limited and [by invitation only](#term:invitation-only) [2438](#cite:2438).
unsolicited_note: Applications are taken only in the dated application periods of its local [grant](#term:grant) [requests for proposals](#term:open-call) [2438](#cite:2438).
how_to_approach: Take the eligibility quiz and apply online through the CyberGrants portal during an application period; applicants register for NPO Hub (formerly FrontDoor) and accept ACH payments [2437](#cite:2437) [2438](#cite:2438).
cycle: 2026: Basic Needs and Income Creation, 2/2/2026 - 3/2/2026, status updates in June, 2026; Stable Housing and Empowering Communities, 5/18/2026 - 6/29/2026, status updates in September, 2026 [2438](#cite:2438). Neighborhood Builders 2026 applications are closed and the next cycle opens Spring 2027 [2438](#cite:2438) [2437](#cite:2437).
typical_grant: "Grant amounts vary by market and organization size."; no multi-year grants through the local grant process; funding no more than once in a calendar year, with rare exceptions [2438](#cite:2438).
geography: The bank's local markets in the United States [2439](#cite:2439).

name: Wells Fargo and the Wells Fargo Foundation
what_it_funds: Three priorities: financial opportunity, housing access and affordability, and small business growth [2440](#cite:2440).
who_it_funds: Organisations with tax-exempt status under [section 501(c)(3)](#term:section-501c3), qualified governmental agencies, tribal entities, and public schools or school systems; not individuals, political entities, labor or fraternal groups, recreational teams, for-profit businesses or travel-related programmes [2441](#cite:2441).
unsolicited_note: "Wells Fargo and the Wells Fargo Foundation have implemented an invitation process." [2441](#cite:2441)
how_to_approach: An organisation invited to apply uses the invitation code it is given to reach the online application portal; the page describes no way to request an invitation [2441](#cite:2441).
cycle: No timetable is given on the pages read [2441](#cite:2441).
geography: National and local [grants](#term:grant) in the United States [2440](#cite:2440).

name: The Home Depot Foundation
what_it_funds: On 2026-10-04 its [grants](#term:grant) page listed three programmes: Veteran Housing Grants, Retool Your School and Path to Pro Grants [2442](#cite:2442). Veteran Housing Grants fund "new construction or rehabilitation of multifamily, permanent supportive housing for veterans" [2443](#cite:2443).
who_it_funds: For Veteran Housing Grants: [501(c)(3)](#term:section-501c3) organisations in good standing with the IRS for at least five years, with a current operating budget of at least $300,000 and audited financial statements for the past three years [2443](#cite:2443). Eligibility for the other two programmes was not on the pages read [2442](#cite:2442).
unsolicited_note: Proposals are taken for named programmes in dated cycles; the pages read state no general policy on [unsolicited requests](#term:unsolicited-request) [2442](#cite:2442) [2443](#cite:2443).
how_to_approach: Submit a project proposal at foundation.homedepot.com, choosing the Veteran Housing Grant application for the cycle wanted [2443](#cite:2443).
cycle: Veteran Housing Grants, 2026 proposal deadlines: Cycle 1, 12/12/2025 (final determinations April 2026); Cycle 2, 3/20/2026 (August 2026); Cycle 3, 7/3/2026 (December 2026) [2443](#cite:2443).
typical_grant: "Awards typically range from $100,000 to $500,000." [2443](#cite:2443)

name: Lowe's Foundation
what_it_funds: Skilled trades training: the Gable [Grants](#term:grant) programme "directly supports community and technical colleges and nonprofit organizations" to train 250,000 tradespeople by 2035 "through a $250 million investment" [2444](#cite:2444).
who_it_funds: Community and technical colleges, community-based non-profit organisations and national non-profit organisations; the detailed eligibility guidelines are in a document this sweep did not read [2444](#cite:2444).
unsolicited_note: Open application for community and technical colleges only: "Opens in March for community and technical colleges"; "Opens in August for community-based nonprofits (invite only)"; the September round for national non-profits is also invite only [2444](#cite:2444).
how_to_approach: Apply through the Lowe's Foundation Gable Grants online portal in the window for the applicant's category [2444](#cite:2444).
cycle: March for community and technical colleges; August for community-based non-profits, by invitation; September for national non-profits, by invitation; the page gives no dates [2444](#cite:2444).

name: Google for Nonprofits (in-kind programme)
what_it_funds: Products, not cash: "Google for Nonprofits provides access to these Google products at no charge", among them Google Workspace for Nonprofits, Google Ad [Grants](#term:grant), the YouTube Nonprofit Program and Google Earth and Maps [2446](#cite:2446) [2445](#cite:2445).
who_it_funds: A non-profit charitable organisation in good standing; not a governmental entity, a hospital or healthcare organisation, or "a school, academic institution, or university" [2445](#cite:2445).
unsolicited_note: Enrolment is open to any eligible organisation that passes verification; this is an in-kind programme run by the company, not a grant from a foundation [2446](#cite:2446).
how_to_approach: Apply on the programme site and be verified as a non-profit organisation by Goodstack; review takes 2-14 working days [2446](#cite:2446).
cycle: Rolling [2446](#cite:2446).
geography: Available in 180+ geographies [2446](#cite:2446).

name: Microsoft nonprofit grants and discounts (in-kind programme)
what_it_funds: Software and cloud services as [grants](#term:grant) and discounts: "Eligible nonprofits may access discounted pricing on commercial cloud offers and some on-premise offers" [2447](#cite:2447).
who_it_funds: In the United States: non-profits with [501(c)(3)](#term:section-501c3) status, public libraries, public museums and named kinds of health facility; not governmental organisations or agencies, schools, colleges, universities, public utilities, financial institutions, professional, commerce and trade associations, sports organisations, or political or labor groups [2447](#cite:2447). Paid employees and unpaid executive staff may use grants and discounts; volunteers and temporary staff may use discounts only [2447](#cite:2447).
unsolicited_note: Open to any organisation that meets the eligibility rules; this is an in-kind programme run by the company, not a grant from a foundation [2447](#cite:2447).
how_to_approach: Check eligibility on Microsoft's non-profit site; the page read does not give the registration steps or the size of the grants [2447](#cite:2447).

name: Foundation for the National Institutes of Health
what_it_funds: The FNIH "creates and leads alliances and public-private partnerships that advance breakthrough biomedical discoveries" and convenes partnerships between the [NIH](#term:nih), academia, life science companies and patient advocacy groups [2448](#cite:2448).
who_it_funds: The page read describes partnerships and fundraising and names no [grant](#term:grant) programme for outside applicants [2448](#cite:2448).
unsolicited_note: Not stated on the page read [2448](#cite:2448). "Established by Congress in 1990, the FNIH is a not-for-profit [501(c)(3)](#term:section-501c3) charitable organization"; it raises private funds from individuals, corporations, foundations and philanthropic organisations [2448](#cite:2448).
how_to_approach: No application route is given on the page read [2448](#cite:2448).

pending_changes.text: A federal [forecast](#term:forecast), CDC-RFA-CD-27-0067, with an estimated post date of September 30, 2026 and still shown as forecasted on 2026-10-04, would pay administrative costs of the National Foundation for [CDC](#term:cdc) under section 399G of the Public Health Service Act: one expected award, estimated total funding $6,250,000, estimated close date December 1, 2026 [2451](#cite:2451).

name: CDC Foundation
what_it_funds: Public health programmes run with partner money: "an independent nonprofit created by Congress to establish philanthropic and private-sector partnerships"; it uses [requests for proposals](#term:open-call) "to sub-grant funds received for a specific project" [2449](#cite:2449) [2450](#cite:2450).
who_it_funds: Each request for proposals names who may respond: providers of products or services, eligible non-profit or governmental organisations, or a consultant or independent contractor [2450](#cite:2450).
unsolicited_note: "We are not an endowed foundation, and we do not accept or respond to [unsolicited proposals](#term:unsolicited-request)." [2450](#cite:2450)
how_to_approach: Respond to an open request for proposals on the foundation's page [2450](#cite:2450).
cycle: Per request; open on 2026-10-04: Healthy Native Babies Project, due October 9, 2026; Technical Advisor - Laboratory Capacity Building, due October 9, 2026; Early Career Public Health Scholars in Maternal-Fetal Medicine, due October 23, 2026 [2450](#cite:2450).

name: National Fish and Wildlife Foundation
what_it_funds: NFWF "provides funding on a competitive basis to projects that sustain, restore and enhance our nation's fish, wildlife and plants" [2453](#cite:2453).
who_it_funds: "Federal, state, and local governments, educational institutions and nonprofit organizations are welcome to apply for matching [grants](#term:grant)." [2454](#cite:2454)
unsolicited_note: Funding is awarded through posted [requests for proposals](#term:open-call); the pages read do not address [unsolicited proposals](#term:unsolicited-request) in words [2453](#cite:2453) [2454](#cite:2454).
how_to_approach: Find an open request for proposals on the grants page and submit a [pre-proposal](#term:pre-application) or full proposal through Easygrants, NFWF's application system [2453](#cite:2453) [2454](#cite:2454).
cycle: Per programme; five request cycles were open on 2026-10-04, among them Chesapeake Bay Stewardship Fund, Southeast Michigan Resilience Fund, Acres for America, Hurricane Response Marine Debris Removal Fund and Hawai'i Conservation Program [2453](#cite:2453).
indirect_costs: An applicant with a valid federally [negotiated indirect cost rate agreement](#term:nicra) may use it; an organisation without one may use a [de minimis rate](#term:de-minimis-rate) of up to 15% of [modified total direct costs](#term:mtdc); NFWF reserves the right to scrutinise proposals with indirect rates above 15% [2466](#cite:2466).
